Signalsmith Stretch 1.4.0
https://github.com/Signalsmith-Audio/signalsmith-stretch
Commit a670068d9aeb64913331d5cc29337b19a457a7df

Signalsmith Linear 0.6.4 (Stretch's declared dependency)
https://github.com/Signalsmith-Audio/linear
Commit de55e6a50ffcf6f8f43f649692d94691c7025151

Opt-in CatLive changes, enabled only by Apple/JarasPreparedClip:
- signalsmith-stretch.h retains raw input and overlap-add history during inaudible neutral
  warmup, and batches output between unchanged processing steps. Analysis is restored from
  that history at the next spectral block when rate/pitch processing becomes necessary.
- signalsmith-linear/stft.h performs identity synthesis directly from windowed PCM during
  that warmup, retaining overlap-add and normalisation for later live pitch/rate changes.
  FFT processing remains in use for changed spectra and unsupported window configurations.
Tests compare batched output bit for bit, and identity synthesis within FFT rounding error,
including seeks, stereo, changing input/output block sizes and live pitch/rate transitions.
Apple playback enables the FFT Accelerate backend from the same Linear commit
(platform/fft-accelerate.h). Windows uses the same-revision PFFFT backend (platform/fft-pffft.h) with the
vendored single-precision SSE implementation in Windows/ThirdParty/PFFFT.
The DSP preset and spectral algorithm are unchanged.
Both projects are MIT licensed. See LICENSE-stretch.txt and LICENSE-linear.txt.

CatLive additionally opts into CATLIVE_SIGNALSMITH_STATE_COPY on Apple and Windows. It copies
streaming histories between identically configured processors while retaining each
destination's FFT plans and allocated buffers. Shared source results fork through
this operation before an item's rate, pitch, timing or loop diverges. Neither the
DSP preset nor the synthesis algorithm is changed. SharedStretchAudioTests compares
the resulting PCM against independent processors at 44.1/48 kHz, including live
edits, different callback sizes, seeks, loops and stop/restart.

Windows ClipAudio uses the same history-fork operation for identical source renderings.
Per-item gain, pan, fades, effects, routing and transport heads remain independent.
ClipAudioReadTests compares pooled and independent PCM through divergence, seeks and tempo edits.

The spectral bands now use contiguous input, history, output and energy arrays.
Constant rotations are prepared once, and stereo prediction has a fixed-channel
implementation. These changes retain the preset and spectral calculations;
the Intel PCM comparison is bit-identical through changing pitch values.
Unmapped frequency prediction reads the corresponding band directly.

process() also accepts an optional absolute input-frame clock and tempo ratio.
Apple prepared playback uses this for direct time stretching, so splitting a
converter pull into a prefix and suffix cannot round the tempo differently.
The default four-argument calls keep their original input/output-count mapping.
ParallelPreparedAudioTests and SharedStretchConverterTests compare split,
independent and shared PCM through live tempo/pitch edits.

The PFFFT adapter destructors release their buffers directly. Upstream resize(0)
allocates an aligned zero-length buffer, which otherwise leaks on destruction.
FFT arithmetic and normalization remain unmodified.

Windows also enables CATLIVE_SIGNALSMITH_BATCH_OUTPUT: output spans between
unchanged processing steps replace the one-sample output loop. The MSVC
reference comparison is bit-identical through stereo, seeks, pitch/rate edits
and varying input/output sizes.
